name: Ceramides

lead: Ceramides are waxy lipids that make up roughly half of the lipid matrix of the outer skin layer. Moisturizers containing ceramides, often with cholesterol and fatty acids, are used to repair barrier damage, ease dryness and support skin affected by eczema or retinoid irritation.
Clinical trials generally show improved barrier function and hydration compared with simple emollients, though the advantage over other well-made moisturizers can be modest.

paras: Topical ceramides help replenish the intercellular lipid lamellae in the stratum corneum, which reduces transepidermal water loss and restores the barrier against irritants and allergens.
They are among the best-tolerated skincare ingredients, with rare allergic reactions to other formulation components. They are over the counter and benefits depend heavily on the full formula.
